extracted_claims.text: Under the original AI Act text (as adopted 2024), high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were to become subject to obligations 36 months after entry into force, i.e. applying from 2 August 2026.

The Commission proposed a Digital Omnibus on AI, adopted 19 November 2025, to extend the timeline for applying high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months, tying application to confirmation that needed standards/tools are available.

A political agreement on the AI Omnibus (Digital Package on Simplification) was reached by Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and the Omnibus Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026, amending the AI Act's timeline (resulting in Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as applicable from 27.07.2026, and referenced as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 by some secondary sources).
Following the AI Omnibus entering into force, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply (enter into application) from 2 December 2027.

The obligations for high-risk AI systems that are classified as high-risk because they are safety components/embedded in products covered by Annex I Union harmonisation legislation apply from 2 August 2028.

Article 113 of the consolidated AI Act text (as of 27 July 2026) provides that Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (with the exception of Article 6(5)) shall apply from a date described as '2 December 2027' per the amended timeline, while the Regulation as a whole 'shall apply from 2 August 2026' for provisions not otherwise specified.

The AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 guidance states that, without prejudice to Article 5 prohibitions, the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems (other than legacy ones) placed on the market before 2 August 2026 only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date.

The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026) similarly states the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems placed on the market before 'the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113' if subject to significant design changes thereafter, without naming a specific date.

The EU AI Act Service Desk timeline page lists 2 December as a milestone related to new prohibitions and an Article 50(2) transition deadline, and separately lists 2 August 2027 for Member State AI regulatory sandboxes.

A legal-analysis implementation timeline page (undated, appears to reflect pre-Omnibus law) states that 'the remainder of the AI Act starts to apply' on 2 August 2026, except Article 6(1), and that operators of certain pre-existing high-risk systems are covered from that date if subject to significant design changes.

Several commentary/legal-analysis sources describe 2 August 2026 as the (then-current or still-cited) deadline for Annex III high-risk AI obligations, with full compliance for high-risk AI systems expected by 2027.

A news/blog source dated April 9, 2026 describes August 2, 2026 as the date on which the AI Act's 'most consequential obligations' for high-risk/Annex III systems take effect, not reflecting the later Omnibus extension.
Providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III must meet requirements in Articles 8 to 15 of the AI Act and complete a conformity assessment before placing a system on the market.
Annex III lists eight categories of AI use cases that can be classified as high-risk; it is not itself a list of AI systems automatically deemed high-risk.

A commentary source frames 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as 'backstop dates,' noting that if the Omnibus amendments were not approved and enacted before 2 August 2026, the high-risk provisions would, as a matter of current law, apply from that date.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The original AI Act, as adopted in 2024, set 2 August 2026 as the date for high-risk AI obligations under Annex III to apply (high confidence). However, a "Digital Omnibus on AI," adopted by the Commission on 19 November 2025 and agreed by Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, extended this timeline; following the Omnibus Regulation's entry into force on 27 July 2026, Annex III obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk AI systems embedded as safety components in products covered by Annex I Union harmonisation legislation (high confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
Under the AI Act as adopted in 2024, high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were to become subject to obligations 36 months after entry into force, applying from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Digital Omnibus and Legislative Amendment
The Commission proposed a Digital Omnibus on AI to extend the application timeline for high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months, tying application to confirmation that necessary standards and tools are available (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). Council and Parliament reached political agreement on the Omnibus on 7 May 2026, and the Omnibus Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026, amending the AI Act's timeline (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [Consilium](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Current Applicable Dates
Following the Omnibus's entry into force, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Obligations for high-risk AI systems classified as such because they are safety components embedded in products under Annex I Union harmonisation legislation apply later, from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

The consolidated Article 113 text (version dated 27 July 2026) provides that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (excluding Article 6(5)) apply on the amended timeline, while the Regulation generally applies from 2 August 2026 for other provisions (medium confidence) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Relatedly, the AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 guidance addresses "legacy" high-risk systems placed on the market before the Chapter III application date, covering them only if they undergo significant design changes thereafter (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)); the EUR-Lex consolidated text mirrors this without naming an explicit date, instead cross-referencing Article 113 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

Multiple sources dated before the Omnibus's entry into force, or undated and apparently reflecting pre-Omnibus law, still cite **2 August 2026** as the applicable deadline for Annex III obligations (low confidence) ([ResponsibleAI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)). This is superseded by post-Omnibus EU guidance confirming **2 December 2027**. One commentary source frames the later dates as "backstop dates," suggesting the 2 August 2026 date would only apply as a matter of law if the Omnibus had not been enacted before that date (low confidence) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

Secondary sources refer to the Omnibus as "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," but this citation is not corroborated by official EU sources (EUR-Lex, Consilium, Digital Strategy), which do not provide this regulation number (medium confidence conflict). It remains unclear whether the Commission's "confirmation of standards/tools availability" is a precondition still pending for the 2 December 2027 date, or whether that date is now fixed regardless.

## Knowledge Gaps
- The official EUR-Lex regulation number for the Omnibus Regulation remains unconfirmed by primary sources.
- Whether amended Article 113 explicitly states "2 December 2027" or whether this is derived by cross-reference is unclear from the consolidated text structure.
- How Article 111's "significant design changes" provision interacts with the new 2 December 2027 date is not explicitly specified in available guidance.
- Whether any transparency, registration, or conformity-assessment obligations under Articles 8–15 take effect earlier than the general Annex III date remains unresolved.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The original AI Act, as adopted in 2024, set 2 August 2026 as the date for high-risk AI obligations under Annex III to apply (high confidence). However, a "Digital Omnibus on AI," adopted by the Commission on 19 November 2025 and agreed by Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, extended this timeline; following the Omnibus Regulation's entry into force on 27 July 2026, Annex III obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk AI systems embedded as safety components in products covered by Annex I Union harmonisation legislation (high confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
Under the AI Act as adopted in 2024, high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were to become subject to obligations 36 months after entry into force, applying from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Digital Omnibus and Legislative Amendment
The Commission proposed a Digital Omnibus on AI to extend the application timeline for high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months, tying application to confirmation that necessary standards and tools are available (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). Council and Parliament reached political agreement on the Omnibus on 7 May 2026, and the Omnibus Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026, amending the AI Act's timeline (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [Consilium](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Current Applicable Dates
Following the Omnibus's entry into force, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Obligations for high-risk AI systems classified as such because they are safety components embedded in products under Annex I Union harmonisation legislation apply later, from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

The consolidated Article 113 text (version dated 27 July 2026) provides that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (excluding Article 6(5)) apply on the amended timeline, while the Regulation generally applies from 2 August 2026 for other provisions (medium confidence) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Relatedly, the AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 guidance addresses "legacy" high-risk systems placed on the market before the Chapter III application date, covering them only if they undergo significant design changes thereafter (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)); the EUR-Lex consolidated text mirrors this without naming an explicit date, instead cross-referencing Article 113 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

Multiple sources dated before the Omnibus's entry into force, or undated and apparently reflecting pre-Omnibus law, still cite **2 August 2026** as the applicable deadline for Annex III obligations (low confidence) ([ResponsibleAI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)). This is superseded by post-Omnibus EU guidance confirming **2 December 2027**. One commentary source frames the later dates as "backstop dates," suggesting the 2 August 2026 date would only apply as a matter of law if the Omnibus had not been enacted before that date (low confidence) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

Secondary sources refer to the Omnibus as "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," but this citation is not corroborated by official EU sources (EUR-Lex, Consilium, Digital Strategy), which do not provide this regulation number (medium confidence conflict). It remains unclear whether the Commission's "confirmation of standards/tools availability" is a precondition still pending for the 2 December 2027 date, or whether that date is now fixed regardless.

## Knowledge Gaps
- The official EUR-Lex regulation number for the Omnibus Regulation remains unconfirmed by primary sources.
- Whether amended Article 113 explicitly states "2 December 2027" or whether this is derived by cross-reference is unclear from the consolidated text structure.
- How Article 111's "significant design changes" provision interacts with the new 2 December 2027 date is not explicitly specified in available guidance.
- Whether any transparency, registration, or conformity-assessment obligations under Articles 8–15 take effect earlier than the general Annex III date remains unresolved.
